thread:
maya_ml: starting galene-20b int4 canary on dedicated pool (nv4). initial perf looked fine but after ~150s we started seeing memory spikes and OOMs on 2/10 hosts. anyone seeing similar?
eli_runtime: can you paste the launch args and batching config?
maya_ml: config snippet:
```
model: galene-20b
quant: int4
batching:
  max_new_tokens: 128
  prefer_prefetch: true
prefetch: aggressive
worker: dedicated-nv4
```
maya_ml: log excerpt from host-07:
```
[2026-03-19T14:22:10Z] kv_cache_alloc failed: out of memory
[2026-03-19T14:22:10Z] mem_fragmentation: 0.63 -> 0.91
[2026-03-19T14:22:10Z] evict_slots: 0 -> 12
[2026-03-19T14:22:10Z] serving: session 0x7fa3b2 timed out while allocating KV
```
pranav_infra: mem_fragmentation ~0.9 is worrying. looks like repeated prefetch + int4 alignment causing wasted pages. could be allocator + kernel interaction.
audrey_eval: on the eval side, quant quality looks stable on short form, but p95 latency jumps ~80% after warmup which may affect SLAs for chat flows.
eli_runtime: hypothesis: int4 kernels change block sizes so the GPU allocator ends up with many small free ranges; prefetching warms large KV caches that aren't packed well. combined with high max_new_tokens drives RSS up.
maya_ml: quick repro steps I used: run local stress generator (200 concurrent sessions) with same config -> OOM after ~200s. lowering max_new_tokens to 64 prevented OOM in the same test.
pranav_infra: experiments to try: set prefer_prefetch: false, reduce max_new_tokens to 64, enable kv_trim_threshold: 0.6, and add an eviction jitter so slots don't align. also collect per-slab fragmentation metrics.
maya_ml: running a canary with prefer_prefetch=false + max_new_tokens=64 now. will report.
ci-bot: deploy 1719987700 canary to pool-galene started by maya_ml :rocket:
maya_ml: early results: prefer_prefetch=false + max_new_tokens=64 eliminated OOMs in 10/10 runs at 200 conc. p95 latency improved vs canary baseline but token-efficiency dropped ~5% (less batching).
audrey_eval: please run our long-form eval (stories-200) vs the non-quant baseline. we need to catch regressions in coherency. quant may be hiding under short-generation metrics.
eli_runtime: action items: 1) sweep max_new_tokens {64,96,128} 2) run prefetch on/off 3) instrument allocator slabs and add fragmentation delta alert 4) add auto-fallback to fp16 on OOM path (soft fallback)
pranav_infra: I'll add kv_trim_threshold and eviction jitter as defaults for galene canary pool and push a small allocator metric exporter. also will add a canary-level automatic fallback rule for repeated OOMs.
maya_ml: thanks — i'll run the eval sweep and upload traces + flamegraphs. will create ticket with logs and link here. tagging @pranav_infra and @audrey_eval for follow-ups :+1:
pranav_infra: noted, assigning infra follow-up.
maya_ml: will update later today with the eval results and perf traces.
